# KS-910 — Wednesday's task for Ornith, BASH_PATCH (one comment line; written 20:13 on 2026-09-16 from the files at develop M55 `48e65c435` — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` lines 34–52 read (the ticket's `:49-51`, unmoved at this tip); `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` leg 12 (`:506-523`) and leg 14 (`:544-635`) read; `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` modes `:53-59` and run loop `:221-230` read; every `Leg 12`/`leg 12` mention in both files listed — exactly five, and only `pre_push_hook_base.test.sh:49` is false) — **KAM RULED 2026-09-16 09:53 (option 2): "keep leg 12 as reachability (CI runs the suites), correct the comment; close on the comment fix (polish)".** PRE-MEASURED in a scratch clone (see the raise notes).

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`pre_push_hook_base.test.sh:49` says **"Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push"** and credits leg 12 with the red a commit-signing developer would get. Leg 12 runs `run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached` (`preflight.sh:521`), which only proves a suite is REACHABLE and exits before the run block — it executes no cell. The leg that RUNS every shell suite on a gated push is **leg 14** (`preflight.sh:544` `step "14/15  Every shell test suite must actually RUN"`, `:631` a bare `bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`), added by #806 on 2026-09-11, five days after this comment was written. Kam ruled: keep leg 12 as reachability, correct the comment. **This task: line 49 becomes a sentence that calls leg 12 reachability and names leg 14 as the leg that runs the suite, plus one new shell suite proving the false wording is gone, the corrected wording is present, and the comment's next line and the suite's syntax are untouched.** NOT in this task: `:50-51` (still true — leg 14 does run the suite), any code, `preflight.sh`, `run-shell-suites.sh`.

## The exact change — ONE ONE-LINE REPLACEMENT in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh`
E1 — line 49 (context: line 48 is `#` alone, line 50 is `# who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at` — copy both from the file as context):
```
-# Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push, so anyone
+# Leg 12 of the preflight only proves this suite is REACHABLE (it runs no cell); leg 14 RUNS it on every gated push, so anyone
```
The `+` line is byte-exact — copy it; it is ONE physical line; do not touch any other line; do not add a trailing comment.

## The test — CREATE THE NEW FILE `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base_leg_comment.test.sh`

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base_leg_comment.test.sh`

bash 3.2. It lives under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/` beside the reference and READS the subject at `$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` (it never runs it). Its shape is the reference `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh` (full content in `files[...]`): `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, a header comment, `set -uo pipefail`, `TOTAL_CELLS=`, `HERE`/`REPO_ROOT` from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, the set-but-empty refusal, the `[ -f ]` / `[ -r ]` FATAL lines, `pass=0; fail=0`, `ok()` / `bad()`, and the totals + INCOMPLETE guard + `exit`. No temp dir is needed — nothing is written.

**Reproduce the file below EXACTLY as written — every line, in order.** Do not invent a helper, do not rename a variable, do not reword a message. Every value a cell reads is assigned FIRST, above the first cell. The file contains no backslash anywhere; keep it that way. **Your diff for this file is a NEW-FILE diff: `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base_leg_comment.test.sh`, ONE hunk header `@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@`, then EVERY line with a leading `+` (a blank line is a lone `+`) — no context lines, no `-` lines: you are not diffing the reference.**

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for the leg-12 comment in pre_push_hook_base.test.sh (KS-910)
# =============================================================================
# Preflight leg 12 runs `run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached`: it proves every
# suite is REACHABLE and executes no cell. Leg 14 is the leg that RUNS them. The
# KS-883 comment said leg 12 "reaches" the suite on every gated push, crediting
# the red to a leg that never runs it. Kam ruled (2026-09-16 09:53): keep leg 12
# as reachability, correct the comment. These cells pin the corrected wording.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base_leg_comment.test.sh
#        HOOK_BASE_SUITE=/path/to/other/copy bash ...   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=4

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
if [ "${HOOK_BASE_SUITE+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$HOOK_BASE_SUITE" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: HOOK_BASE_SUITE is set but EMPTY - refusing to silently grade the shipped file." >&2
  exit 2
fi
SUBJ="${HOOK_BASE_SUITE-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: pre_push_hook_base.test.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: HOOK_BASE_SUITE is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { echo "  ok   $1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { echo "  FAIL $1"; echo "     $2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

stale_hits="$(grep -c -F 'Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite' "$SUBJ" || true)"
fix_hits="$(grep -c -F 'leg 14 RUNS it on every gated push' "$SUBJ" || true)"
anchor_hits="$(grep -c -F 'who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at' "$SUBJ" || true)"

# CELL 1 - red at the tip
if [ "$stale_hits" -eq 0 ]; then ok "the false claim that leg 12 reaches this suite on every gated push is gone"
else bad "the false leg-12 claim is still present" "hits=$stale_hits"; fi

# CELL 2 - red at the tip
if [ "$fix_hits" -eq 1 ]; then ok "the comment names leg 14 as the leg that runs this suite"
else bad "the corrected leg-14 wording is not present exactly once" "hits=$fix_hits"; fi

# CONTROL CELL 3 - green on both trees
if [ "$anchor_hits" -eq 1 ]; then ok "CONTROL the signed-commits sentence is still there"
else bad "CONTROL the signed-commits sentence moved or vanished" "hits=$anchor_hits"; fi

# CONTROL CELL 4 - green on both trees
if bash -n "$SUBJ"; then ok "CONTROL pre_push_hook_base.test.sh parses (bash -n)"
else bad "CONTROL pre_push_hook_base.test.sh does not parse" "bash -n failed"; fi

echo ""
echo "  $pass passed, $fail failed (of $TOTAL_CELLS cells)"
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  echo "  INCOMPLETE - $((pass + fail)) of $TOTAL_CELLS cells ran"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
```

CELL 1 and CELL 2 are red at the untouched tip **by assertion** (`stale_hits` is 1, `fix_hits` is 0 — both assigned above the cells, nothing unbound, nothing crashes). CONTROL CELL 3 and CONTROL CELL 4 are green on both trees: line 50 is not edited, and a comment edit cannot break `bash -n`.

## Where (parsed into the checklist — every **must change** line must appear as a `-` line in your diff)
* `:49` — **must change**: `# Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push, so anyone`
* `:50` — (correct) `# who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at` — stays

## Output
Exactly ONE ```diff block with TWO files: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` (one hunk), then `--- /dev/null` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base_leg_comment.test.sh` (one `@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@` hunk, all `+`); paths repo-relative; blank context lines keep their leading space.

## Premises (measured)

Every factual claim the `+` line and the new suite assert or rely on, each read at `48e65c435` with `git show 48e65c435:<file>` on 2026-09-16 (20:1x) unless another instrument is named.

1. **"Leg 12 of the preflight only proves this suite is REACHABLE (it runs no cell)"** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:506` `step "12/15  Every shell test suite must be REACHED by the runner (KS-731 / QA F-800-07)"` and `:521` `if ! run_delegated bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached; then`. `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh:56` `--check-unreached) MODE="check" ;;`; the check block `:80-144` ends in `exit 1` or `exit 0` at `:143`, before the run loop at `:221`. The file's own `preflight.sh:554` agrees: "Leg 12 is `--check-unreached`, which exits before the run block."
2. **"leg 14 RUNS it on every gated push"** — `preflight.sh:544` `step "14/15  Every shell test suite must actually RUN (KS-731 / QA FR-800-03)"`, `:631` `if ! env "${env_clear[@]}" bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh; then` (no argument → `MODE="run"`, `run-shell-suites.sh:53`/`:57`). The runner globs `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/*.test.sh` (`:48-51`, `:62-69`) and runs every hit (`:221-230`, no exclusion list); `git ls-tree 48e65c435 Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/` lists `pre_push_hook_base.test.sh`. Every leg is reached: the only `exit` between `:150` and `:690` is the step-header/TOTAL_LEGS mismatch abort at `:173`, and all fifteen headers read `/15` with `TOTAL_LEGS=15` (`:130`). Stated residual: if leg 14's environment measurement comes back empty (`:620-626`) the suites are NOT run and the leg sets `fail=1`, so that push is blocked — every push that PASSES has run the suite. Leg 14 landed in `ec2d8c4ca` (#806, 2026-09-11; `git log -S`), after this comment (`3bfbd06eb`, 2026-09-06).
3. **"gated push"** — not new: the term is already in the `-` line and is the ticket's own; the hook runs the preflight for any push touching `Blockchain/Dev` and unconditionally when no base can be computed (`.githooks/pre-push:195`, `:203`).
4. **Lines `:50-51` stay true** ("anyone who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook") — they describe why KS-883 isolates git config for the whole file (`:34-52`); with leg 14 executing the suite in the pushing developer's environment (only slot variables are cleared, `:627-631`), a regression of that isolation would red on the push. Not edited.
5. **Kam's ruling** — Linear KS-910 (read 20:07) carries the ticket's option 2 "correct the comment to 'reachable'"; the ruling text "keep leg 12 as reachability (CI runs the suites), correct the comment; close on the comment fix (polish)" is quoted from the commission, not re-read from a Linear comment (the ticket has no comments). "CI runs the suites" measured true: GitHub Actions run 34961722314 (`GET /actions/runs/34961722314/jobs`), step `All shell test suites (KS-666 / KS-731 — globbed, not listed)` executed → `failure`; `.github/workflows/pr-security-gates.yml:100` `run: bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`. The `+` line does NOT assert this.

Claims deliberately NOT made: anything about CI or GitHub Actions; any leg count other than the two leg numbers.

## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **Pre-measured before this brief was written** (scratch clone `git clone --shared` of the Secuura checkout, `checkout 48e65c435`, by script file): the new suite alone at the tip → `2 passed, 2 failed (of 4 cells)`, rc 1, both reds by assertion; with the one-line edit → `4 passed, 0 failed (of 4 cells)`, rc 0; the completeness arm proven to fire on the GREEN tree (CONTROL CELL 4 cut out → `INCOMPLETE - 3 of 4 cells ran`, rc 1). The product itself is a suite, and the checker's B6 will run it as a sibling (its own header names its basename): `pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` read `28 passed, 0 failed` before and after the edit. The file is 58 lines and carries no backslash (`grep -c` = 0).
- **Which comment is false, measured.** Every `Leg 12` / `leg 12` line at the tip, in both files: `preflight.sh:139` (a measured instance of leg 12's runner skipping in a non-git checkout — true), `:545` ("Leg 12 proves every suite is FINDABLE. Nothing proved any of them RUNS" — true), `:554` ("Leg 12 is `--check-unreached`, which exits before the run block" — true, `run-shell-suites.sh:80-144` exits in check mode), `:654` ("`--check-unreached` already enforces exactly this for SUITES (leg 12)" — true), and `pre_push_hook_base.test.sh:49` — **false**, the ticket's sentence, at the ticket's line. `run-shell-suites.sh` carries no leg-12 claim.
- **Why the corrected line names leg 14 and not CI.** The ticket (written when the preflight had 12 legs) says "no shell test suite runs on a gated push". That is stale at this tip: leg 14 (`ec2d8c4ca`, #806, 2026-09-11) runs the bare runner, which loops over every globbed suite (`run-shell-suites.sh:221-230`, roots `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__` + `systemTest/__tests__`, no exclusion list), so the red `:50-51` promises is real — only its attribution to leg 12 is false. Kam's "(CI runs the suites)" is also measured true (GitHub Actions run 34961722314, `PR Security Gates (KS-168)`, step `All shell test suites (KS-666 / KS-731 — globbed, not listed)` executed on 2026-09-15 and concluded `failure`), but a code comment that names a CI workflow's state would restate a fact the repo's docs currently record the opposite way (see below); the leg-14 fact is in the same tree and cannot drift out from under it silently without this suite's CELL 2 noticing a rename.
- **Adjacent stale comment, NOT touched — a Kam-class reconciliation.** `preflight.sh:548-550` says "GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27; see CONTRIBUTING.md), so BOTH `run: bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` workflow steps are dormant." It sits under "Measured at e26cfce2b:" (a dated measurement, true on 2026-09-04 when Actions was 100% `startup_failure`), but as present tense it is now contradicted by the run above and by Kam's own 09:53 words. `CONTRIBUTING.md` asserts the retirement in five places (`:419-423`, `:449-450`, `:485-486`, `:494-504`, `:603-604`). Whether the 2026-08-27 retirement ruling is superseded is Kam's call; the KS-789 r2 brief raises the same question.
- **The ticket's option-1 gap is closed by leg 14, not by this ticket.** Worth saying in the close-out comment so nobody reopens KS-910 for option 1: the suites DO execute on every gated push today (leg 14), and in CI.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for .githooks/pre-push — base resolution (KS-854)
# =============================================================================
# The defect this exists for: on a FRESH CLONE the gate skipped entirely and
# said nothing.
#
# `git clone` creates only the default branch locally, so `develop` exists
# solely as `refs/remotes/origin/develop`. The hook did a bare
# `git merge-base develop HEAD` into a `$(…)` with stderr discarded; that
# failed, `base` was empty, `changed` stayed empty, and
# `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returned SUCCESS before leg 1. Push rc 0, in
# seconds, with no `[pre-push]` line at all — no gate, and no signal there was
# no gate. Reported as F-850-02 by the #840 gate, which hit it by accident.
#
# It is the same shape as KS-676 (a CVE scan reporting clean having examined
# nothing) and KS-853 (leg 9 passing a planted violation): AN EMPTY RESULT READ
# AS A PASS. So the cases below assert on whether the hook ANNOUNCED ITSELF,
# not on the preflight's verdict — "did the gate run" is the property that was
# lost, and a suite that only checked exit codes would have passed throughout
# (the broken hook exits 0, and so does a healthy skip).
#
# Every fixture pushes to a LOCAL BARE REMOTE. Nothing here reaches GitHub.
# The preflight is stubbed to an instant `exit 0` on purpose: this suite tests
# the hook's DISPATCH, not the preflight's legs, and a real preflight would
# make the fixtures depend on node_modules and a running stack.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh
#        HOOK_SH=/path/to/other/pre-push bash …   (to test a different copy)
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# KS-883 — ISOLATE THE GIT CONFIG FOR THE WHOLE FILE, NOT JUST THE FIXTURE BUILD.
#
# This export used to live inside `build_fixture`'s subshell, so it isolated the
# BUILD and nothing else: the CONTROL and CASES 1-3 ran under whatever global
# git config the operator has. Measured with `commit.gpgsign = true` and an
# unusable `gpg.program`, which is an ordinary developer configuration:
#
#   hostile global config -> 4 passed, 2 failed   (CASE 1 falsely RED)
#   GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null -> 6 passed, 0 failed
#
# and the run printed `fatal: failed to write commit object` twice. CASE 1 was
# red for a reason that has nothing to do with the hook, and CASE 2's `ok` was
# VACUOUS in the same run — its commit failed too, so the push it asserts on
# carried no docs change at all. A green cell there meant nothing.
#
# Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push, so anyone
# who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at
# their own config.
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
HOOK="${HOOK_SH:-$REPO_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push}"

if [[ ! -f "$HOOK" ]]; then
  echo "FATAL: pre-push hook not found at $HOOK" >&2
  exit 2
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks854.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0
fail=0

ok()   { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad()  { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Build a fixture repo. $1 = dir, $2 = "with-develop" | "no-develop".
# Leaves you with: a bare origin, and a clone whose ONLY local branch is main.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" mode="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root"
  (
    # Inherited from file scope (KS-883); repeated here so the fixture stays
    # hermetic if this function is ever lifted into another suite.
    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
    git init -q --bare -b main "$root/origin.git"
    git init -q -b main "$root/seed"
    cd "$root/seed"
    git config user.email t@t.t; git config user.name t
    mkdir -p Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight systemTest docs
    echo base > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
    echo docs > docs/readme.md
    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho "[preflight] ran"\nexit 0\n' \
      > Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh
    : > systemTest/slot-target.sh
    # KS-989: the hook now invokes the systemTest formatting gate, so the fixture
    # must provide one — the same reason preflight.sh is stubbed above. A STUB,
    # not the real script: this suite is about base resolution, and the real gate
    # has its own suite (systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh).
    # It records that it was invoked (CASE 7) and fails on demand (CASE 8).
    mkdir -p systemTest/scripts
    cat > systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh <<'GATE_STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
{ printf 'argv=%s\n' "$*"; [ "${1:-}" = "--all" ] || cat; } > "$root/.gate-invoked" 2>/dev/null
[ -f "$root/.gate-should-fail" ] && { echo "[format-gate] stub refusing on demand" >&2; exit 1; }
exit 0
GATE_STUB
    chmod +x systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh
    git add -A; git commit -qm init
    if [ "$mode" = with-develop ]; then
      git branch develop
    fi
    git remote add origin "$root/origin.git"
    if [ "$mode" = with-develop ]; then
      git push -q origin main develop
    else
      git push -q origin main
    fi
    cd "$root"
    git clone -q "$root/origin.git" fresh
    cd fresh
    git config user.email t@t.t; git config user.name t
    mkdir -p .githooks
    cp "$HOOK" .githooks/pre-push
    chmod +x .githooks/pre-push
    git config core.hooksPath .githooks
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONTROL FIRST — the fixture really does reproduce the fresh-clone shape.
# Without this, every case below could be passing for the wrong reason.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c0" with-develop
(
  cd "$WORK/c0/fresh"
  branches="$(git branch --format='%(refname:short)' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  git rev-parse --verify develop >/dev/null 2>&1 && local_dev=YES || local_dev=NO
  git rev-parse --verify origin/develop >/dev/null 2>&1 && remote_dev=YES || remote_dev=NO
  # KS-881: cut the branch the CASES cut, and report ITS upstream. The fixture's
  # shape is not only "no local develop" — it is also "the branch under test has
  # no upstream", and that half was invisible in this line.
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  up="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' 2>/dev/null)"
  [ -n "$up" ] || up=NONE
  printf '%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$branches" "$local_dev" "$remote_dev" "$up"
) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null
IFS='|' read -r c0_branches c0_local c0_remote c0_up < "$WORK/c0.out"
if [ "$c0_local" = NO ] && [ "$c0_remote" = YES ] && [ "$c0_up" = NONE ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — the fixture is a real fresh clone: local branches [${c0_branches% }], develop local=NO remote=YES, upstream=NONE"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the fixture is a real fresh clone" \
      "expected local develop NO + origin/develop YES + upstream NONE; got local=$c0_local remote=$c0_remote upstream=$c0_up"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 1 — THE REGRESSION. Fresh clone, no local develop, branch with NO
# upstream, carrying a real Blockchain/Dev change. The gate MUST announce.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c1" with-develop
out1="$(
  cd "$WORK/c1/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  # KS-881 — ASSERT THE PRECONDITION THIS CASE RESTS ON.
  #
  # `--no-track` is what makes this branch have NO upstream, which is what sends
  # the hook down the base-resolution path under test. Nothing asserted it.
  # Measured: drop `--no-track` and the branch tracks origin/develop, `changed`
  # comes from `@{upstream}` instead, the gate runs for an unrelated reason, and
  # the suite goes 2/4 -> 4/2 AT THE PARENT HOOK — this case passes against the
  # very bug it exists for, and the CONTROL cannot see the loss.
  if git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/x has an upstream; --no-track is not in effect"
  fi
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change"
  # KS-883 — the commit must have LANDED, or everything below asserts on a push
  # that carried nothing. A signing failure is silent to a grep of push output.
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  git push origin feature/x 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q '\[pre-push\]'; then
  ok "fresh clone + no upstream + a Blockchain/Dev change → the gate RUNS and says so"
else
  bad "fresh clone + no upstream + a Blockchain/Dev change → the gate RUNS and says so" \
      "no [pre-push] line: the gate skipped silently (KS-854)"
fi

# KS-881 — the precondition really was absent, ASSERTED rather than assumed.
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 1's branch really has no upstream (the --no-track precondition holds)" \
      "feature/x tracks a remote branch, so this case exercises the @{upstream} path, not the base-resolution path it exists for"
else
  ok "CASE 1's branch really has no upstream — the precondition is asserted, not assumed"
fi

# The preflight really was invoked — otherwise case 1 proves nothing.
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "…and the preflight was actually invoked, not merely announced"
else
  bad "…and the preflight was actually invoked, not merely announced" \
      "the [pre-push] line appeared but the preflight never ran"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 2 — the fix must not become "always run". A docs-only push still skips.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c2" with-develop
out2="$(
  cd "$WORK/c2/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b docs/x --no-track origin/develop
  echo more >> docs/readme.md

else

else

build_fixture "$WORK/c10" with-develop
out10="$(
  cd "$WORK/c10/fresh"

    cd "$WORK/c10/seed"
    git checkout -q develop

    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop equals origin/develop, so it is current, not stale"

  git diff --name-only origin/develop HEAD | grep -q '^Blockchain/Dev/' \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the branch itself carries a Blockchain/Dev path, so the gate would run for the ordinary reason"

  ok "CASE 10 — a stale local develop is IGNORED for base selection, and the hook says so (KS-991)"
else

fi
if printf '%s' "$out10" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  bad "CASE 10 — a docs-only push on a CURRENT base SKIPS the preflight" \
      "the preflight ran: the stale local develop inflated the diff with the trunk's Blockchain/Dev change (the KS-991 defect)"
else
  ok "CASE 10 — a docs-only push on a CURRENT base SKIPS the preflight, despite the stale local develop"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 11 — the KS-991 fix must not become "always skip". The SAME stale local
# develop, but the branch DOES touch a Blockchain/Dev file: origin/develop is

    cd "$WORK/c11/seed"

    git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change on the trunk, not yet in local develop"

  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/stale@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/stale has an upstream; the base-resolution path is not exercised"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor develop origin/develop 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop is not an ancestor of origin/develop, so the stale-ref rule cannot apply"

# (KS-877)

# banner's `${BUILD_LIST[*]}` with `BUILD_LIST[*]: unbound variable` under

# expansion after it does not. And `${BUILD_LIST[*]:-}` alone only moves the
# death 55 lines down to the parallel loop's `"${BUILD_LIST[@]}"` — measured —
# so the shape that holds is a guard on `${#BUILD_LIST[@]}` that names the
# table and exits before either.
#
# docker is NEVER run: a stub on a private PATH records every call and exits 0,
# so the control cells can prove the working path still builds without a
# daemon. The empty table is produced by a fixture COPY of the subject whose
# heredoc body is stripped — the table is a literal inside the script, so
# there is no other way to reach the path — and the copy's row count is
# asserted 29 -> 0 before the cell is scored.
#
# Round 2 (KS-877, the tier-2 gate's F1): CELL 3 was RED on the repository's CI
# (ubuntu, bash 5.x) while green on macOS — `docker-build.sh`'s `((RUNNING++))`
# exits 1 when RUNNING is 0, and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` (COMPAT item 45) kills the
# script on it; bash 3.2 does not. CELL 4 pins the construct's ABSENCE statically
# (this box has no bash >= 4.1; CI's CELL 3 is the runtime instrument) and CELL 5
# proves the fix does not swallow a genuine build failure. The summary line
# carries the cell count (`(of N cells)`) and the run FAILS if fewer cells ran.
#

[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: docker-build.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks877.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Data rows of the SERVICES_TABLE heredoc in a script: tab-separated, not a
# comment. The same predicate service_names() applies.
table_rows() {
  sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$1" \
    | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# Build a fixture project root around a copy of the script under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = table: intact | emptied
# The copy lives at <root>/scripts/docker-build.sh so the script's own
# `PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."` resolves to the fixture root.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" table="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/scripts" "$root/bin" "$root/services/auth"
  printf 'FROM scratch\n' > "$root/services/auth/Dockerfile"
  if [ "$table" = emptied ]; then
    # Strip every line between the heredoc's opening and closing markers.
    sed "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/{//!d;}" "$SUBJ" > "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  else
    cp "$SUBJ" "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  fi
  # docker stub: records every call, succeeds.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\nexit 0\n' "$root"; } > "$root/bin/docker"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker"
}

# Run the copy with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_build() {
  local root="$1"; shift
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"; cd "$root" && bash scripts/docker-build.sh "$@" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
build_calls() { if [ -f "$1/docker_calls.txt" ]; then grep -c '^docker build' "$1/docker_calls.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-877. THE REGRESSION. An EMPTY table must be refused by name —
# "no services matched", naming SERVICES_TABLE — with NO `unbound variable`
# and no build attempted. Asserted on rc = 1 AND the ABSENCE of the
# unbound-variable death AND the PRESENCE of the message naming SERVICES_TABLE
# AND 0 builds. rc alone cannot discriminate base from head (both exit 1),
# which is why the other three clauses exist; it is asserted so that a guard
# that prints the message and then exits 0 still reds (the gate's Tk). The row
# count is a precondition: a copy that still has rows would pass the pre-fix
# script and say nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" emptied
rows_subj="$(table_rows "$SUBJ")"; rows_copy="$(table_rows "$WORK/empty/scripts/docker-build.sh")"
if [ "$rows_subj" -lt 1 ] || [ "$rows_copy" -ne 0 ]; then
  bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
      "precondition broken: subject rows=$rows_subj (expected >=1), emptied copy rows=$rows_copy (expected 0) — the cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_empty="$(run_build "$WORK/empty" all)"
  if [ "$rc_empty" = 1 ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/empty")" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE ($rows_subj rows -> $rows_copy) is refused by name — 'no services matched', naming SERVICES_TABLE — with no 'unbound variable', 0 builds, rc=$rc_empty"
  else
    bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
        "rc=$rc_empty, unbound variable present=$(grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo YES || echo no), message present=$(grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), table named=$(grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/empty"), last lines: $(tail -2 "$WORK/empty/out.txt" | sed 's|.*/scripts/||' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL (the working path, one service). The intact table with
# `auth` must still print `Services:  auth`, build it once via the stub, report
# BUILD OK and exit 0. Without this, CELL 1 could pass by a guard that refuses
# every list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/one" intact
rc_one="$(run_build "$WORK/one" auth)"
if [ "$rc_one" = 0 ] && grep -q '^  Services:  auth$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" && grep -q '\[auth\] BUILD OK' "$WORK/one/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/one")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q -- '-f services/auth/Dockerfile' "$WORK/one/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' prints 'Services:  auth', builds it once (-f services/auth/Dockerfile), BUILD OK, rc 0"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' still builds it once and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_one, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/one"), output: $(grep -v '^=*$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (the working path, every service, the parallel loop). The
# intact table with `all` must build every row via the stub and exit 0 — the
# path whose re-index guard (`${#PIDS[@]}`) the file's own comment documents,
# exercised under bash 3.2 with instant builds so the loop's empty-array case
# is actually reached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" intact
rc_all="$(run_build "$WORK/all" all)"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj):" "$WORK/all/out.txt" && grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/all/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/all")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/all/out.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj), rc 0, no unbound variable"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_all, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/all") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED' "$WORK/all/out.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — KS-877 round 2 (the gate's F1). The subject has NO bare
# arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement (`((X++))` / `((X--))` on a line
# of its own). Such a command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0 — a
# post-increment yields the OLD value, so `((RUNNING++))` at RUNNING=0 "fails"
# — and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` exits on it (bash COMPAT item 45: "Bash-4.1 …
# exits when any command fails, not just a simple command or pipeline").
# bash 3.2 (macOS) does not, which is why CELL 3 was green here and RED on CI's
# ubuntu (run 34743050388: `rc=1, builds=0 of 29` — the script died after
# backgrounding ONE build). This is a STATIC pin, honest about being one: the
# runtime pin is CELL 3 on a bash >= 4.1, i.e. CI. The positive control inside
# the cell proves the grep can fire (a here-string holding `((X++))` -> 1).
# `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`: BSD grep.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARITH_RE='^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$'
arith_control="$(printf '  ((X++))\n' | grep -cE "$ARITH_RE" || true)"
arith_hits="$(grep -nE "$ARITH_RE" "$SUBJ" || true)"
arith_count="$(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | grep -c . || true)"
if [ "$arith_control" != 1 ]; then
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "instrument cannot fire: the positive control read $arith_control (expected 1) — the cell is not scoring the subject"
elif [ "$arith_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement — ((X++)) exits 1 at 0 and bash >= 4.1 set -e dies on it (control fires: $arith_control)"
else
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "count=$arith_count (control=$arith_control): $(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | sed 's/^\([0-9]*\):[[:space:]]*/:\1 /' | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — KS-877 round 2, the MASK CONTROL. A run where ONE build genuinely
# fails must still land in `FAILED (1)` with rc 1 and the summary printed —
# the counter fix must not swallow a real failure. A second stub records the
# call, then exits 1 when its args name services/auth/Dockerfile (asserted
# unique among the table's rows). On bash 3.2 this reads the SAME before and
# after the fix — that IS the control: the fix changes nothing 3.2 can see
# except the arithmetic status; on CI (bash 5.x) it exercises the fixed loop
# under a genuine failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/onefail" intact
{ printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\ncase "$*" in *services/auth/Dockerfile*) exit 1;; esac\nexit 0\n' "$WORK/onefail"; } > "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
chmod +x "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
auth_rows="$(sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$WORK/onefail/scripts/docker-build.sh" \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $2 == "services/auth/Dockerfile"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$auth_rows" -ne 1 ]; then
  bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
      "precondition broken: $auth_rows table rows resolve to services/auth/Dockerfile (expected exactly 1) — the failing stub cannot be aimed"
else
  rc_onefail="$(run_build "$WORK/onefail" all)"
  if [ "$rc_onefail" = 1 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))):" "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && grep -q 'FAILED (1):' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && grep -q '^    auth$' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && ! grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt"; then
    ok "MASK CONTROL — with the auth stub exiting 1, 'all' still runs every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))), FAILED (1): auth, rc 1"
  else
    bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
        "rc=$rc_onefail, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED\|All builds' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-877 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE — %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
